title: Registry Forensics: User Activity
description: Extract evidence of user actions from UserAssist, RecentDocs, USB artifacts, and more.

slides.title: The User Footprint 👣
slides.content:
# Registries That Spy on Users

Several registry keys track user interactions:
- **UserAssist**: Records GUI‑based program launches with run counts and last execution time.
- **RecentDocs**: Lists recently opened files (by extension).
- **TypedURLs**: URLs typed into Internet Explorer.
- **MountPoints2**: Connected USB devices and mapped network drives.
- **Shellbags**: Folder view settings (which folders were opened).

We'll dissect each one.

quizData.question: Which registry key contains information about programs launched via the Windows GUI (with run count)?
quizData.explanation: UserAssist stores GUI‑based program execution data, including launch count and last execution time.

slides.title: UserAssist Key 🔍
slides.content:
Located under `HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Explorer\UserAssist`.

It contains subkeys like `{CEBFF5CD-...}` and `{F4E57C4B-...}`. Each value name is a ROT13‑encoded (Win10+) or plain (Win7) program path. The binary data encodes:
- Run count (bytes 4‑7)
- Last run time (FILETIME at offset 60 or 72 depending on version).

Decoding these reveals how many times a program was launched and when it was last used.

slides.title: Parse UserAssist with RegRipper
slides.content: Use RegRipper to extract UserAssist entries.
slides.codeSnippet:
rip.pl -r NTUSER.DAT -p userassist
# Output: program path, run count, last run time.

quizData.question: On Windows 10, UserAssist value names are ROT13‑encoded to obfuscate the program path.
quizData.explanation: Yes, Windows 10 applies ROT13 to the executable path to make it less human‑readable, but it's trivial to decode.

slides.title: RecentDocs & OfficeDocs 📄
slides.content:
`HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Explorer\RecentDocs` tracks recently opened files, sorted by extension (`.txt`, `.pdf`, etc.). Each value is a binary string containing the file name, and the MRU (Most Recently Used) order.

`HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Office\<version>\<App>\File MRU` records files opened in Office applications.

These entries remain after the file is deleted, providing evidence of document access.

quizData.question: The 'R' in MRU stands for ___.
quizData.explanation: MRU = Most Recently Used; it tracks the order of file access.

slides.title: USB Device History 🖱️
slides.content:
## Mounted Devices and Portable Storage

`HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Enum\USBSTOR` lists every USB storage device ever connected. Each subkey is a device ID, containing vendor, product, and serial.

`HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows Portable Devices\Devices` shows similar info.

`HKCU\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Explorer\MountPoints2` records which drive letters were assigned and contains a drive serial number.

The `Properties` value inside each device subkey of `Enum\USBSTOR` includes the last connection time (LastWrite time of the key itself).

These keys collectively prove if a USB drive was plugged in, when, and what it was.

quizData.question: Which registry key stores the serial number of connected USB storage devices?
quizData.explanation: USBSTOR enumerates all USB mass storage devices, with the serial number embedded in the device instance ID.

slides.title: Network History & Typed URLs 🌐
slides.content:
`HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Internet Explorer\TypedURLs` stores URLs that were typed into the IE address bar (not search queries).

`HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Explorer\Map Network Drive MRU` records mapped network shares.

These complement browser history artifacts for network activity.

slides.title: Pro Tip 🚀
slides.content:
## Use Registry Explorer for Quick Triage

Loading a hive into Registry Explorer lets you visually browse and see LastWrite times. For bulk analysis, `regripper` or `KAPE` with registry modules are essential.
